text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- A separatist Kurdistan Worker Party (PKK) militant died when a bomb exploded in her hand in the coastal holiday resort of Bodrum.
MILLIYET
- President Suleyman Demirel reassures the continuation of secularism in Turkey in his visit to Canakkale province.
- It is expected that the anti-Islamist government will announce a new minimum wage on Monday.
HURRIYET
- The former Islamist-led government appointed 59,000 supporters to key official posts in its year-long rule.
- An official report reveals that 81 percent of women in Istanbul do not work.
YENI YUZYIL
- Conservative opposition party True Path Party says it will not support a military-sponsored education plan to expand compulsory education to eight year.
- Turkish Airlines boosted its passengers numbers with a 20 percent discount in domestic flights. It targets to have flown 600,000 people by the end of 1997.
CUMHURIYET
- Turkey plans to expand "suitcase trading" taking place in Istanbul to the Turkish Cypriot sector of Cyprus.
RADIKAL
- Nine died and 52 were injured in traffic accidents throughout Turkey.
DUNYA
- Banks began opening branches in the southeastern Turkey after a huge dam project brought the region to life.
ZAMAN
- Polityical mistakes prevent Turkey from properly exploiting its oil reserves.
